candidates.text:
NFL Week 2 Preview

The second week of the season is among my favorites, because it’s correction week. Here’s what I’m looking at on this slate:

- Ben Johnson vs. Brian Flores is the best interdivision coaching matchup in the league currently. The Bears offense has the raw talent edge in said matchup.

- If Bill Belichick was calling a game against Caleb Williams, I think he’d try to make him play from the pocket while selectively blitzing, and when he did I think he’d send heat at Caleb’s throwing side, and he’d probably dial up more pressure with speed. Flores is not Belichick, but he’s scaled back his blitz rate against Johnson in the past and he’s on the short list of defensive coordinators that I could see really coloring outside the lines against Johnson/ Caleb.

- Kevin O’Connell vs. Dennis Allen is another excellent coaching matchup, where in this phase the Vikings have the more talented roster.

- Kyler Murray being out reduces the ceiling of Minnesota’s offense, but I’ll also say that Carson Wentz’s relief appearance against Green Bay last week is the best I’ve seen him play in years. That said, I need to see Dennis Allen limit Carson Wentz at home after what I saw in Carolina last week, where short to intermediate in breakers were basically free for the whole game.

- If Minnesota loses with Wentz at the controls, that’s not a big deal to me, the pressure is more on Chicago to put this one away against a division rival, and no one in the NFC North is an easy out.

- Broncos vs. Jaguars is the most interesting game on the slate for me because I have these two teams in the same relative bucket, where I went with Denver having a more successful 2026 and winning this game when I mapped things out this offseason.

- Denver’s pass rush has a trench advantage in this contest, and their offensive line should be able to mitigate the strength of Jacksonville’s defense, which is their front. In fact, I could see Denver having a sneaky good game on the ground in this matchup. I’m very curious to see if Davis Webb leans into that after bombing last Monday night.

- Trevor Lawrence is the X-Factor in this contest, where I am a week away from outright saying that I’d rather have him than Drake Maye long-term, which is one of the reasons I’m really looking forward to this contest.

- Speaking of Maye, he draws another quality front and a Steelers’ defense that he struggled against/ lost to last season. One that added talent this offseason, but it looks like it will be without Joey Porter Jr. Maye is a nice young player, but he has not played very well against real NFL defenses. I’ll be curious to see how he bounces back coming off what might have been his worst game as a Patriot to date last week.

- The other side of the ball is where I see New England having an edge, as you get Mike Vrabel’s defense, coming off a loss they had very little to do with, against a Steelers offense that quite simply let Cooper Rush’s Falcons hang around all day last week. Keep in mind that Pittsburgh also scored defensively on an outlier play by T.J. Watt in their 20-13 win over the Falcons last week.

- I have defended Aaron Rodgers over the past two years, as he’s had plenty of good to impressive games for a quarterback over the age of 40 during that span. He has not been at the peak of his powers, nor should anyone have expected him to be given his age, but he’s been solid or better more often than not. I did not want him to return this season because I thought that might change, and I’m concerned that I’m right after Week 1.

- Houston’s defense is coming off a shootout that they lost, where they’ll now get a second high-powered offense manned by another elite quarterback in Joe Burrow, who is a bit banged up but is playing. The Texans pass rush/ secondary combo against Burrow/ Ja’Marr Chase/ Tee Higgins is as good of a heavyweight matchup as there is.

- Nico Collins is out, which gives C.J. Stroud a very thin group of pass catchers against an otherwise beatable Bengals secondary. What’s interesting for me here is Cincinnati’s front had a pretty good game against Tampa last week, and the Bucs have a significantly better offensive line than Houston does. I could see the Bengals front being impactful in Houston, if not the difference in this contest.

- Cowboys vs. Commanders isn’t quite a loser leaves town matchup, but it’s close. Dak Prescott is coming off a pretty middling game, where I could see the Cowboys offense bouncing back against a well-coached, but mediocre at best Commanders defensive roster.

- On the other side of things, we just saw Jaxson Dart play ultra efficient football against the Cowboys’ defense. Jayden Daniels could carry this game, giving this contest some very high scoring potential if both quarterbacks are on.

- The Rams are in the most obvious correction spot on the slate, especially Matthew Stafford who is coming off one of the worst games I’ve ever seen him play.

- I’m throwing out the Australia game for the purposes of evaluating the Rams, but Stafford did look a little old in that matchup, so the primary thing I’m looking for here is was that just a veteran quarterback coming off an outrageously long flight, or did father time catch up to the future Hall of Famer a bit this offseason? I expect Stafford to be fine, but I have my eyes on that.

- The Giants pass rush has an abnormal amount of talent at edge, but that group did not have much of an impact against Dallas. Is that a group that feasts on bad offenses/ bad tackles, or can they be a factor against a contender? If you’re a Giants fan, I’d have my eye on that.

- The other thing you’re looking for is what Jaxson Dart does in this spot. So far, Dart has been pretty good when he’s not facing what I’m going to start calling chaos pressure. The great ones succeed despite it, the good but not great guys do not. Myles Garrett is out, which obviously reduces the chances of the Rams front four derailing this game, even though Aaron Donald returns to the NFL for Monday Night Football.

- For me, Dart can’t really do anything that I’d flag as a real long-term negative in this matchup, apart from taking another front side hit on the chops that he doesn’t see. That’s a pattern I’d like to see him break. But if the Rams defense plays well, and Stafford returns to form, if Dart keeps New York in this game, that’s very encouraging.

- The 49ers are better at every single position group than Miami, where running back is the only one that’s close. San Francisco also has the far better, more accomplished coach, creating an environment that would require a catastrophe for them to lose given how many advantages they have.

- I saw very little out of Miami in Week 1, which is what I expected, but my biggest concern in this matchup is if Malik Willis has to play from behind for much of this game, he takes a lot of bad sacks. Further, San Francisco, arguably, has the best linebacker group in the league, which will limit his rushing upside. Like I said, I think it will require a catastrophe for the 49ers to lose here.

- Last week was the best I’ve ever seen Zay Flowers look, where I wondered aloud on two separate occasions last Sunday if he might be a top 5 receiver. I’ve always liked him, but that blew my top off a little last week. Flowers being doubtful is generally unfortunate, but he had a potential smash spot against New Orleans.

- That makes Lamar Jackson’s job tougher. If any quarterback in the league doesn’t need a difference making wide receiver to have a plus game, it’s Jackson. That said, given that Flowers absence makes Jackson’s legs his far and away biggest asset in this game, paired with the presence of the immortal Derrick Henry coming off one of his signature monster games, I wonder if New Orleans, who has been well coached since Kellen Moore took over last year, goes into the archives and tries to do their best to duplicate Brian Flores’ blitz-heavy approach that has shut down Jackson in the past. That’s easier said than done, but I’d put New Orleans on the short list of teams that might try it.

- Tyler Shough had one of the oddest games you’ll ever see last week, where he was genuinely bad for 40 minutes, but finished with over 400 yards passing after the overtime period. Jessie Minter’s Ravens are a significantly tougher out than the current Detroit Lions defense, that we just saw get annihilated by Josh Allen Thursday night.

- One thing on my radar is Baltimore has lost a few improbable games in September over the years.

- I’ve been pretty enthusiastic about the Jets long term prospects for a while, with the concern that they’d be just good enough to not be able to get a true future at quarterback in this year’s draft, as you can’t really trade up with teams that need a quarterback themselves. That said, I think Green Bay wins here and Jordan Love has a pretty high ceiling in this matchup.

- If the Packers get beat up a bit by Geno Smith, who actually has a pretty good supporting cast, I’ll be concerned about Green Bay’s defense given some of the changes they’ve endured this offseason.

- I also wonder if this sets up for a Breece Hall game, as Green Bay has been a run sieve in previous seasons in the recent past.

- You could say Baker Mayfield single handedly lost a winnable game in Cincinnati last week with his three fumbles. If he does not play significantly better in his revenge game against the Browns, who were atrocious last week, I will have many questions.

- Deshuan Watson is the only NFL player I’ll point blank say I don’t like, not only because of his off-field stuff, because he’s been a moron both before and after about it. He’s also had the strangest career drop off imaginable, as he looked like a future Hall of Famer in Houston, yet throughout his career in Cleveland he has been a guy that is a fringe NFL quarterback. I don’t recall any other instance that’s similar to this. He’s playing behind a bad line against a solid Bucs front, but this is also the kind of matchup where if he has anything left, he has to show some of it here.

- I would hope this is a KC Concepcion week, but it’s also a good spot for Jerry Jeudy.

- I thought the Jets were going to score some points on the Titans, but I could not believe that Tennessee did not keep up at all. I also cannot believe how little progress their offensive line has made, given the draft capital and financial investments they’ve made in that group. I also, as I’ve said many times, had zero enthusiasm for the Saleh/ Daboll hires. Facing this Eagles defense looks like a bad situation for this offense unless they can completely transform within a week.

- I have had good experiences over the years with Falcons fans, which is part of the reason I genuinely feel bad for them that they are opening the season with two games from third string quarterback Cooper Rush. I will say this though, if Atlanta ended up being the worst team in the league this season, where they could get a No. 1 overall pick quarterback, that may actually be the best thing for this franchise because they do have some pieces. I don’t think that’s going to happen, but if they end up being bad in the league’s worst division, I hope it’s that level bad.

OMO-AGEGE CONDEMNS ATTACK ON NDC MILLION-MAN MARCH, DEMANDS IMMEDIATE INVESTIGATION

I strongly condemn the violent and unprovoked attack on the peaceful One Million-Man March organised by the Delta State Chapter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) yesterday in Uvwie Local Government Area.

2. The march, led by our Governorship Candidate, Chris Iyovwaye, was a peaceful and lawful expression of political support. Thousands of enthusiastic Deltans came out to participate. There was no justification whatsoever for the violence that followed.

3. The sequence of events is particularly disturbing. The march was originally scheduled to begin at Angle Park in Warri South Local Government Area. After our members gathered there, they were told by persons identified as APC supporters to leave because, according to them, the APC had a rally at the location. Following discussions with the police, our members moved to the next junction, around the Total filling station in Warri.

4. At the Total filling station, APC supporters allegedly approached our members again and claimed that the government had instructed them not to allow the NDC march to proceed through their area in Warri South. Our members were subsequently asked to move towards the traffic-light junction in Uvwie.

5. As soon as the procession reached the Uvwie junction, it was allegedly attacked by APC supporters in the area. Despite the attack, our members managed to move through to Ugborokoko, where they were allegedly attacked from different directions.

6. It was at Ugborokoko, according to accounts from participants, that gunshots were fired at the procession. Our members nevertheless managed to move on. When they reached Jakpa Road, they were attacked again. It was during this confrontation that Collins, alias “Black Moses,” was allegedly disarmed of an AK-47 rifle and subsequently handed over to the police.

7. The violence continued at Urhuomarho, where the procession reportedly came under a full-scale attack. More than 100 people were reportedly injured during the various incidents and are receiving treatment in hospitals.

8. Our supporters bravely stood their ground and, in the course of defending themselves, apprehended one of the attackers, identified as Collins Ogumashe, alias “Black Moses” — a notorious thug in Ugboroke allegedly tasked by the Delta State Government to violently attack and disrupt NDC campaigns in Uvwie.

9. He was allegedly caught in possession of an AK-47 rifle. He was disarmed by a renowned human rights activist, Efemena Umukoro, and has since been handed over to the police. But the information reaching us is that Governor Sheriff Oborevwori has ordered the Commissioner of Police to arrest Umukoro.

10. More than 100 people were reportedly injured in the attack and are receiving treatment in hospitals. These are Deltans who simply came out to participate in a political march. They should never have been subjected to such violence. I extend my solidarity to all those affected and commend the members and supporters of the NDC for their courage and restraint. Despite the attack, they refused to be intimidated and went ahead to complete the march. That determination deserves recognition.

11. Governor Sheriff Oborevwori must also take responsibility. As Chief Security Officer of Delta State, he cannot look away when citizens are attacked while exercising their democratic rights. The buck stops at his table.

12. Delta State has seen enough of political violence. We must not return to the days when thugs determined who could campaign, where political parties could gather, or which political voices could be heard.
